full_judgment: 9. From the plaint it appears that the plaintiff prayed for a decree for permanent injunction restraining defendant Nos. 1 and 2 from changing the polling stations from Debipur Government Primary School to Naldanga School and from Joypur registered non government primary school to Panchapolli Nimna Maddhamik Biddalaya. Such kind of suit can only be filed under section 54 of the Specific Relief Act which clearly provides that a perpetual injunction may be granted subject to the other provisions contained in, or referred to, by Chapter X to prevent the breach of an obligation existing in favour of the applicant whether expressly or by implication. In the second and 3rd parts of said section, obligation arising from contract and the invasion or threat by the defendant to the plaintiffs right to, or enjoyment of, property have been categorised in which injunction can be granted. Those categorisations do not attract the facts of the instant case as disclosed in the plaint as well as the reliefs sought for. Therefore, the first part of section 54 of the Act has to be referred to, to see as to whether any obligation exists in favour of the plaintiff.
